title: Require claim-support check for study-text edits in producer brief
summary: Add a convention to the change producer prompt: when a job's files are under studies/, for every new or reworded statement the producer opens each cited claim id, checks the claim text supports the sentence (including who acts), and lists each changed statement with its claim text in the change description; unsupported statements get a sourced claim in claims.json or are dropped; the changelog never says claims support wording unless they do. Audience: producers and verifiers of study-page jobs.

defaults_applied.how: Criteria check the prompt text and passing checks, not activity.
Convention marked prose-only in the docs file.
One prompt sentence plus a short convention doc and changelog.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Goal: producers editing study text stop adding statements their cited claims do not support; audience is the change producer reading its brief and the verifier checking study-page jobs.

The 'producer brief used when files are under studies/' is the change capability producer prompt (crates/athena-cap-change/prompts/producer.md), as that is where the existing rendered-page convention is carried; no path-conditional brief mechanism exists, so the sentence is written conditionally ('when your files are under studies/').
Study-capability producers (crates/athena-cap-study/prompts/producer.md) are left alone; it has 182 tokens of headroom and the request concerns edit jobs.
Not a refusal rule, so no replay percentage applies; the convention is prose-only, marked as such, with verification by the verifier reading the cited claims.
Environment: none beyond the repository copy.

acceptance_criteria.text: crates/athena-cap-change/prompts/producer.md contains a sentence, conditioned on the job's files being under studies/, that requires the producer to open each cited claim id, check the claim text states what the sentence says including who does the action, and list each changed statement with its supporting claim text in the change description (checked by Grep/Read of the file).

The same prompt says that a statement with no supporting claim must get a sourced claim added to claims.json or be dropped, and that the changelog must not say claims support a wording unless they do.
The prompt text fits the producer (change) token budget (889 of 1200 used); the repository's prompt budget tests pass with the added text.
The convention is written for a stranger in docs/conventions/study-claim-support.md (rule, why, enforcing mechanism or marked prose-only), and the prompt points to it.
No files under studies/ and no Rust source other than test expectations tied to prompt text are changed; CHANGELOG.md has an entry describing the convention.
cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy and cargo test all pass, including prompt structure/mirror checks over the edited prompt and docs.

out_of_scope: Editing any studies/*/model.json, intro.json or claims.json content
Adding a code check that validates claim support
Changing the study capability prompts or the verifier prompts
departures: Prompt-only change with a token budget and mirror checks; slightly cheaper than reference but verification risk from prompt-structure checks.
